title: Linear Neural Networks for Classification
subtitle: Contact session 4 · T1 Chapter 4 · sigmoid + BCE with SGD, softmax + cross-entropy with mini-batch SGD, and metrics

lesson.title: What classification is
lesson.lead: Classification predicts a **discrete class label**; regression predicts a continuous number.

blocks.text: Why not linear regression?
Linear regression outputs any real number, but we need a probability in [0, 1]. A line can predict values below 0 or above 1. **Fix:** squash the output with a function that maps (−∞, ∞) to (0, 1).

lesson.title: Logistic regression = one sigmoid neuron
lesson.lead: Compute z = wᵀx, then **ŷ = σ(z) = P(y = 1 | x)**.

blocks.text: z = wᵀx = w₀ + w₁x₁ + … + w_d x_d          ŷ = σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e⁻ᶻ)
blocks.caption: z is called the logit (pre-activation)

blocks.text: Decision rule
predict 1 if ŷ ≥ 0.5  ⇔  wᵀx ≥ 0;   predict 0 otherwise
blocks.caption: the decision boundary wᵀx = 0 is a hyperplane

blocks.text: Four components: **data** (x, y ∈ {0,1}), **model** (sigmoid neuron), **objective** (binary cross-entropy), **learning** (stochastic gradient descent).

lesson.title: Binary cross-entropy
lesson.lead: Squared error is the wrong loss for probabilities. Use **binary cross-entropy (BCE)**.

blocks.text: ℓ = −[ y log ŷ + (1 − y) log(1 − ŷ) ]          J(w) = (1/N) Σ ℓ⁽ⁱ⁾

items: If y = 1: ℓ = −log ŷ, which is small when ŷ → 1.
If y = 0: ℓ = −log(1 − ŷ), which is small when ŷ → 0.
Confident wrong answers are punished hard: y = 1, ŷ = 0.1 → ℓ = 2.303; ŷ = 0.9 → 0.105.

blocks.text: Why cross-entropy?

items: Comes from maximum likelihood (Bernoulli).
Heavily penalises confident mistakes.
Convex for logistic regression: one global minimum.
Pairs with the sigmoid to give a very simple gradient.

lesson.title: Stochastic gradient descent
lesson.lead: SGD updates the weights using **one random example** at a time.

blocks.text: ∇ℓ = (ŷ⁽ⁱ⁾ − y⁽ⁱ⁾) x⁽ⁱ⁾          w ← w − η (ŷ − y) x
blocks.caption: the same form as the regression gradient: error × input

items: Initialise w = 0 (or small random values).
For each epoch, shuffle the data.
For each example: ŷ = σ(wᵀx), gradient (ŷ − y)x, update w ← w − η∇ℓ.
Optionally monitor the total loss J(w).

head: Batch GD (M3)
SGD (M4)
rows: Online learning; noise can escape sharp minima

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: SGD is more sensitive to η and oscillates near the minimum. The common compromise is **mini-batch** SGD.
The class-1 examples (x = 3, 4) moved toward 1. The class-0 examples are still above 0.5, so more steps and epochs are needed.

blocks.label: Exam tip
blocks.text: Mini-batch and SGD numericals are likely in the paper: **two steps** with the given η, each step showing z, ŷ, error, gradient and new w.

lesson.title: Binary metrics
lesson.lead: Use the **confusion matrix** and pick the metric whose mistakes cost the most.

blocks.text: Accuracy = (TP + TN)/(TP + TN + FP + FN)    Precision = TP/(TP + FP)    Recall = TP/(TP + FN)    F1 = 2PR/(P + R)

head: Metric
Use when
rows: Classes are balanced (misleading if 95% are negative)
False positives are costly (marking real mail as spam)
False negatives are costly (missing a sick patient)

blocks.text: Example: TP = 3, TN = 3, FP = 1, FN = 1 → accuracy = 6/8 = 0.75, precision = 3/4 = 0.75, recall = 3/4 = 0.75, F1 = 0.75.
Split: train 90–99%, validation 10–15% (tune hyperparameters), test 1–10% (final evaluation).

lesson.title: Multi-class: softmax
lesson.lead: K output neurons give K logits; **softmax** turns them into probabilities that sum to 1.

blocks.text: z = Wᵀx  (W is (d+1) × K, one column per class)        ŷₖ = e^{zₖ} / Σⱼ e^{zⱼ}

items: Total parameters: (d + 1) × K.
Each row of Z = XW holds the logits of one example.
Labels are **one-hot**: class 2 of 4 → [0, 1, 0, 0]. This treats classes equally and matches the softmax output.

blocks.label: Implementation tip
blocks.text: Numerical stability: compute softmax(z − max z). It gives the same answer and prevents overflow (the log-sum-exp trick).

lesson.title: Categorical cross-entropy
lesson.lead: The loss depends only on the probability given to the **true** class.

blocks.text: ℓ = −Σₖ yₖ log ŷₖ = −log ŷ_true          J(W) = −(1/N) Σᵢ Σₖ yₖ⁽ⁱ⁾ log ŷₖ⁽ⁱ⁾
With K = 2 it is exactly binary cross-entropy (y₂ = y, y₁ = 1 − y).
∂ℓ/∂z = ŷ − y          ∇_W J_B = (1/B) X_Bᵀ (Ŷ_B − Y_B)

blocks.label: Convention clash
blocks.text: One slide writes ∇ = X_Bᵀ(Ŷ − Y) without 1/B, but the algorithm slide divides by B. Follow the question; if it says nothing, use the average (1/B).

lesson.title: Mini-batch SGD
lesson.lead: Use **B examples per update**: faster than batch GD, steadier than SGD.

blocks.text: iterations per epoch = ⌈N / B⌉          W ← W − (η/B) X_Bᵀ(Ŷ_B − Y_B)
Example: N = 60,000, B = 128 → ⌈468.75⌉ = 469 iterations per epoch; 10 epochs → 4,690 updates.

head: Batch size
Pros
Cons
rows: More updates, better generalisation, escapes sharp minima
Slower convergence, more memory, may generalise worse

items: Initialise W ~ N(0, 0.01).
Each epoch: shuffle, split into mini-batches.
Forward: Z = X_B W, Ŷ = softmax(Z).
Gradient: (1/B) X_Bᵀ(Ŷ − Y).
Update: W ← W − η∇.

blocks.text: Inference
Compute z = Wᵀx, ŷ = softmax(z), predict argmax. Example from the deck: z = (1.2, 2.5, 0.8) → ŷ = (0.187, 0.687, 0.126) → class 2 with 68.7% confidence.

lesson.title: Multi-class metrics
lesson.lead: A K × K confusion matrix: rows are actual classes, columns are predicted; the diagonal is correct.

blocks.text: Deck example: 150 examples, diagonal 45, 38, 44 → accuracy = 127/150 = 0.847.
Precisionₖ = TPₖ/(TPₖ + FPₖ)   Recallₖ = TPₖ/(TPₖ + FNₖ)   (one class vs the rest)
**Top-K accuracy:** correct if the true class is among the K highest probabilities (ImageNet reports top-1 and top-5).

lesson.title: Summary and debugging
lesson.lead: Match the activation and loss to the task, scale features, and check probabilities sum to 1.

head: Symptom
Fix
rows: Lower η, avoid log(0), scale features, stable softmax
Check softmax/loss, one-hot labels; η may be too small
Implementation bug: use the stable softmax
Overfitting: regularise, more data, simpler model

blocks.label: Tips
blocks.text: Sanity check: a tiny dataset should reach 100% training accuracy. Initialise weights small (N(0, 0.01)) to avoid sigmoid saturation; shuffle every epoch.
